title: Hybrid Capacity Accounting and Billing — Ops Playbook
author: Asha Kapoor
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines the end-to-end operational rules, accounting treatments, billing flows, and procurement handoffs for hybrid capacity agreements at Redwood Inference. 'Hybrid capacity' refers to any customer arrangement that mixes reserved (dedicated) capacity, committed spend, and on-demand hosted usage under a single commercial contract. The goal is consistent revenue recognition, timely invoicing, clear procurement linkage, and predictable customer experience across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope:
- Applies to multi-product customer commitments that combine Dedicated pools, hosted API call volumes, and optional burst credits.
- Covers contracts signed from 2028-11-01 onward (legacy agreements are handled under migration procedure, see section "Migration & Reconciliation").
- Intended audience: Finance (RevRec), Billing Ops, Procurement, Legal, Sales Ops, and Customer Success.

Principles:
1. Economic substance over form: revenue recognition follows delivered capacity and consumption, not just invoice timing.
2. Single source of truth: UsageCollector -> UsageWarehouse -> RevenueEngine is canonical pipeline for meter data.
3. Separation of concerns: Procurement owns POs and vendor-like commitments; Finance owns GL mapping and rev rec.
4. Timely customer transparency: Draft invoices available within 48 hours of monthly cutoff; disputes acknowledged within 5 business days.

Key terms and definitions:
- Committed Credit: dollar commitment purchased for a period (monthly/annual) redeemable against usage or Dedicated reservation.
- Reserved (Dedicated) Unit: GPU capacity reserved and billed per the capacity contract; invoiced monthly or upfront depending on contract.
- Burst Credit: short-lived, non-recurring credits for on-demand spikes; expiration rules in section "Credit Lifecycle".

Roles & ownership:
- BillingService: Invoice generation, dunning, payments. Owner: Finance-Billing.
- UsageCollector: Collects per-request telemetry across Hosted and Dedicated routers. Owner: Eng-Platform.
- CommitmentOrchestrator: Matches customer POs to contract terms and issues commitment IDs. Owner: Sales-ops.
- RevenueEngine: Applies rev-rec rules and emits journal entries to LedgerAPI. Owner: Finance-RevRec.
- Customer Success: manages communication for monthly true-ups and usage anomalies.

Accounting & Revenue Recognition Rules (summary table):

| Scenario | Recognition trigger | Timing | GL account | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Upfront prepay for Dedicated (term) | Service delivery over time measured as capacity availability | Straight-line over term or practical performance measure if usage materially differs | Deferred revenue -> Revenue | If customer can use across months, straight-line unless usage-based consumption meets criteria for variable consideration.
| Monthly committed credit (redeemable) | When customer redeems credit (consumption) | At point of consumption | Revenue | Unredeemed credits recognized as deferred revenue and recognized on expiration per contract.
| On-demand hosted usage | Metered at request level | At point of usage (month-end) | Revenue | UsageCollector must reconcile to invoice within 48h of cutoff.
| Cross-product conversion (credit applied to Dedicated) | When system applies credit to invoice | When credit applied against invoice | Revenue/Contra-revenue mapping | Maintain audit trail: CommitmentID + ApplicationEventID.

Billing flow and timing:
1. Daily aggregation: UsageCollector batches per-customer telemetry into UsageWarehouse every 6 hours.
2. Invoice draft window: Monthly cutoff is the 1st of the month 00:00 UTC for prior-month usage; draft invoices produced within 48 hours by BillingService.
3. Approval & finalization: Finance-Billing has 3 business days to approve automated drafts. If manual review required, add 5 business days SLA.
4. Distribution: Final invoices published to Customer Portal (S3 link) and emailed. Payment terms default 30 days net unless contract specifies otherwise.

Procurement handoff & PO mapping:
- All POs must include: Customer legal name, Redwood customer ID, CommitmentID (if exists), PO amount, currency, billing cadence, and any invoice delivery exceptions.
- CommitmentOrchestrator creates a CommitmentID that links the signed contract to all billing events.
- If procurement issues a single PO that covers both Dedicated hardware reservations and variable usage, Sales-Ops must create line-item mapping so statements in BillingService show dedicated vs usage amounts.

Credit lifecycle and expiration rules:
- Standard committed credits expire 12 months from purchase unless otherwise specified in contract.
- Burst credits expire 30 days from issuance.
- Expired credits are moved from deferred liability to breakage revenue per ASC guidance after legal review.

True-up and credit allocation procedure (operational steps):
1. Trigger: At month end, UsageWarehouse emits a Redline Report where actual usage differs from committed levels by >10%.
2. CS notifies customer and opens a True-up ticket in Jira (project: FIN-BILL).
3. Billing Ops runs CommitmentOrchestrator transform to allocate committed credits against usage events.
4. If consumption > commitment: charge usage at overage rates; produce a supplemental invoice for the overage with 15-day payment term.
5. If consumption < commitment: calculate unused committed credit; propose one of: (a) apply credit forward (if contract allows), (b) issue a refund (rare; needs CFO approval), or (c) convert to breakage per contract.
6. Document outcome in the True-up ticket and tag with CommitmentID and InvoiceIDs.

Journal entries & GL mapping (examples):
| Action | Debit | Credit | Comment |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Customer prepays annual Dedicated $120k | Cash | Deferred Revenue | Recognize deferred revenue on receipt; revenue recognized monthly at $10k unless practical performance indicates otherwise |
| Redeem committed credits $5k | Deferred Revenue | Revenue | When customer redeems credits against usage |
| Breakage recognition of expired credits $2k | Deferred Revenue | Misc Revenue (breakage) | Requires legal sign-off and disclosure in denial of refund clause |

Reporting, dashboards and thresholds:
- Daily metrics published to Finance Dashboard (Looker): committed_use_rate, month_to_date_invoice_delta, unredeemed_credit_balance.
- Alert: committed_use_rate < 60% for 14 consecutive days -> triggers CS review.
- Invoice generation SLA: 95% of draft invoices produced within 48 hours of cutoff.
- Billing latency tolerance: invoices finalized <= 10 business days after cutoff for complex contracts; otherwise <= 5 business days.

Example scenarios (worked):
1) Annual Dedicated + usage burst: Customer prepays $360k for 36 GPU-months plus 50k burst credits. RevenueEngine straight-lines the $360k. Burst credits consumed month-of are recognized as usage revenue at consumption.
2) Enterprise commitment with cross-product conversion: Customer buys $200k committed credit. 60% redeemed against Hosted API, 40% applied against Dedicated palette. CommitmentOrchestrator records application events and RevenueEngine recognizes revenue at time of redemption with reference to CommitmentID.
3) Under-consumption true-up: Customer contracted for 100 GPU-hours/month committed; actual average 60 GPU-hours. CS initiates True-up; Finance recommends apply-forward if contract allows; otherwise breakage recognition upon expiration.

Migration & reconciliation (legacy agreements):
- Legacy contracts with inconsistent credit expiry: create migration plan and normalized CommitmentID.
- Run a historical reconciliation job (script: scripts/recon/legacy_to_hybrid.py) to map prior invoices to current GL mapping. Finance-RevRec to approve mapping and communicate to auditors.

Escalation, approvals and exceptions:
- Refunds above $10k require CFO and Legal approval.
- Manual invoice adjustments must include memo with approver and Jira ticket link.
- Exceptions to expiration policy require Legal review and documented business rationale.

Implementation checklist for Billing and Finance teams (technical tasks):
- [ ] UsageCollector: ensure redelivery for missing telemetry >0.1% rate.
- [ ] BillingService: implement CommitmentID column in invoice line items.
- [ ] RevenueEngine: support breakage recognition flag and audit export.
- [ ] CommitmentOrchestrator: add API endpoint POST /commitments/{id}/apply-credit for CS workflows.
- [ ] Finance Dashboard: add committed_use_rate and unredeemed_credit_balance tiles.

Appendix A — Contract language snippets (recommended clauses):
- "Committed Credits: Credits are redeemable for services provided by Redwood Inference during the term and expire twelve (12) months after purchase unless otherwise stated."
- "Breakage: Except as otherwise agreed, unused committed credits at expiration shall be recognized by Redwood Inference as non-refundable breakage and recorded as revenue under applicable accounting standards."

Appendix B — Frequently asked questions:
Q: When do we treat committed credits as variable consideration?
A: If the customer has significant discretion in redemption that creates variability, revenue should be deferred until redemption (point of consumption). For predefined, non-refundable reservations that guarantee availability, consider performance over time. Work with Finance-RevRec.
